The IT provider corpITOp requires a service to manage 5,000 office employees. This service must filter dangerous websites, 
scan downloaded files for malware, and ensure that sensitive data does not leave the network. The service chain includes, 
in order: a <webFilterVF, 4> allocated at the edge, a <malwareScannerVF, 16> located in the cloud, and a <dlpEngineVF, 8> located in the cloud. 
Regarding requirements, it is a mandatory requirement that the latency from <webFilterVF, 4> to the <malwareScannerVF, 16> remains below 10 milliseconds. 
Furthermore, the bandwidth between the <malwareScannerVF, 16> and the <dlpEngineVF, 8> must be greater than 500 Mbps.

The cybersecurity provider secureMailOp requires a service to manage 10,000 corporate mailboxes. This pipeline intercepts incoming emails, 
removes phishing links, analyzes attachments in an isolated environment, and delivers only safe messages to the server. The service chain includes, 
in order: a <mailGatewayVF, 4> allocated at the edge, a <phishingFilterVF, 8> located in the cloud, a <sandboxScannerVF, 16> located in the cloud, and a <safeDeliveryVF, 4> 
node located in the cloud. Regarding requirements, decoding must be applied after the <mailGatewayVF, 4>. Furthermore, the provider prefers to keep the 
latency from the <mailGatewayVF, 4> to the <phishingFilterVF, 8> below 50 milliseconds. It is strictly required that the bandwidth from the <phishingFilterVF, 8> to 
the <sandboxScannerVF, 16> is higher than 100 Mbps. Finally, logging is mandatory before the <sandboxScannerVF, 16>.

The website security provider ddosProtectionOp requires an anti-DDoS defense system to handle 50,000 active web users. This system analyzes incoming traffic,

applied before the <scrubbingFilterVF, 32>. Furthermore, it is strictly required that the bandwidth between the <networkTrafficAnalyzerVF, 8> and the <scrubbingFilterVF, 32> is greater 
than 500 megabps. Additionally, the provider prefers to enforce logging after the <rateLimiterVF, 16>. Finally, it is desired that the latency from the <rateLimiterVF, 16> 
to the <webServerVF, 12> remains lower than 10 ms.

security is mandatory before the <reportGeneratorVF, 8>.

The network security provider secureCryptoOp requires an encrypted traffic analysis service to support 25,000 corporate users. This service inspects HTTPS flows 
without fully decrypting them, using AI to identify malware or botnet patterns. The deployed service chain includes, in order: <trafficSplitterVF, 8> allocated at 
the edge, a <featureExtractorVF, 16> located in the edge, an <aiClassifierVF, 32> located in the cloud, an <alertManagerVF, 4> located in the cloud, and a <policyEnforcerVF, 12> located 
in the cloud. Regarding requirements, decoding is applied after the <trafficSplitterVF, 8>. Furthermore, the provider prefers to keep the total chain hardware lower 
than 80 gigabytes. It is mandatory that the <trafficSplitterVF, 8> and the <featureExtractorVF, 16> are deployed on the same hosting node. Finally, security is enforced 
before the <policyEnforcerVF, 12>.

The government provider govMessagingOp requires a service to manage 50,000 institutional messages. This service receives digital communications,
verifies the electronic signature of the sender, checks its integrity, and archives the message in a legal vault. The deployed service chain 
includes, in order: a <msgReceiverVF, 8> allocated at the edge, a <sigVerifierVF, 16> located in the cloud, an <integrityCheckerVF, 12> located in the 
cloud, and a <legalVaultVF, 32> located in the cloud. Regarding requirements, caching is applied after the <msgReceiverVF, 8>. Furthermore, the provider 
prefers to keep the total chain hardware lower than 100 GB. It is a mandatory requirement that the <sigVerifierVF, 16> and the <integrityCheckerVF, 12> 
operate on the same node. Finally, compression is applied before the <legalVaultVF, 32>.

The gaming provider cloudGamingOp requires a service to manage 40,000 active gamers. This service executes video games on powerful servers 
and sends the video stream to the user, guaranteeing a very low latency to avoid making the game unplayable. The deployed service chain 
includes, in order: a <gameExecutorVF, 32> allocated in the cloud, a <streamPackerVF, 16> allocated in the cloud, and a <deliveryOptimizerVF, 8> allocated 
at the edge. Regarding requirements, encoding is applied after the <gameExecutorVF, 32>. Furthermore, it is strictly required that the latency 
from the <streamPackerVF, 16> to the <deliveryOptimizerVF, 8> remains below 30 ms. Finally, the provider prefers that the <gameExecutorVF, 32> and the <streamPackerVF, 16> operate on dedicated nodes.

streams the video to the user, ensuring very low latency to prevent the game from becoming unplayable. The service chain begins with a

The chain then connects to a <streamPackerVF, 16> hosted in the cloud; this component is also preferred to run on a dedicated node. Finally, 
the traffic is routed to a <deliveryOptimizerVF, 8> hosted at the edge, ensuring that the latency from the <streamPackerVF, 16> to this <deliveryOptimizerVF, 8> remains less than 30 ms.
